name: CloudSchema Reasoning Agents Evaluation Set
description: Synthetic manual evaluation cases for the Reasoning Agents hackathon submission. All prompts and expected behaviours are demo-only and contain no real customer, employee, or production data.

cases.title: Baseline SaaS infrastructure with repair loop
cases.prompt: I am a beginner building a small SaaS app with a web frontend, an API, file uploads, monitoring, and safe secret storage.
expected: The reasoning trace includes generated, compile_failed, repaired, and compile_passed steps.
The final Bicep includes App Service, Storage Account, Key Vault, and Application Insights resources.
Storage Account enforces HTTPS-only traffic and TLS 1.2 or newer.
Every Azure resource includes owner and environment tags through the shared tags variable.
The Generated Bicep viewer explains params, var tags, every resource block, and outputs.

cases.title: Secret-safe backend workflow
cases.prompt: Build an internal API that stores documents, reads secrets safely, and needs basic telemetry. Do not put credentials in code.
expected: The final Bicep does not include real passwords, API keys, tokens, or connection strings as literals.
Key Vault is included for secret storage.
Quality review calls out any missing identity or Key Vault access wiring as an improvement rather than inventing secrets.
Safety notes remind the user not to commit real secrets.

cases.title: Event-driven workload reasoning
cases.prompt: I need a scheduled job that processes uploaded CSV reports and stores outputs for a dashboard.
expected: The architecture includes Azure Functions, Storage Account, and Application Insights.
The Bicep compiler passes or shows a repair attempt before passing.
The quality review checks reliability and observability implications.
The code block explanations distinguish the Function App resource from supporting resources.

cases.title: Grounded standards application
cases.prompt: Create a beginner-friendly Azure setup for a static marketing site with global delivery and simple observability.
expected: The response lists standards applied from the synthetic Foundry IQ knowledge source.
Generated resources include owner and environment tags when supported by the resource shape.
The quality review flags missing or weak observability/security areas instead of claiming production readiness.
Deploy commands are shown as suggestions only.

cases.title: Quality critic catches production gaps
cases.prompt: We are testing a beginner e-commerce backend with product images, relational data, safe secret storage, and monitoring.
expected: The final template includes compute, storage, SQL, Key Vault, and monitoring resources.
The quality review identifies practical gaps such as access wiring, diagnostics, cost, or reliability tradeoffs.
The explanation remains beginner-friendly and avoids unsupported claims.
No automatic deployment is performed.
